claim: Even when models are given expertly written gold editorials (i.e. the algorithm is already solved and explained), they still struggle with implementation on competitive-programming problems, showing pass/fail failure in competitive code arises from both reasoning AND implementation, not a single localizable requirement.
stance_target: competitive programming lacks a clean per-requirement decomposition the way functional/library-call code (BigCodeBench) does
scope_conditions: 83 ICPC-style problems, 19 LLMs evaluated, gold vs generated editorials
quoted_support: even with gold editorials, models continue to struggle with implementation, while the gap between generated and gold editorials reveals a persistent problem-solving bottleneck in specifying correct and complete algorithms

claim: The paper explicitly frames standard pass/fail competitive-programming metrics as insufficiently diagnostic, motivating an editorial-based (reasoning-vs-implementation) evaluation axis instead of a per-test-case partial-credit axis.
stance_target: how the field currently diagnoses competitive-programming failure when binary pass/fail is uninformative
quoted_support: Beyond pass/fail metrics, we diagnose reasoning errors by comparing model-generated editorials to gold standards using expert annotations and validate an LLM-as-a-judge protocol for scalable evaluation.
